thread:
sam-support: FYI forwarded a customer report — rerank endpoint seeming to return inconsistent order compared to scores. Customer attached snippets + logs. They say it works in Python but TS client returns wrong ordering.
sam-support: customer snippet (TS):
```ts
const resp = await Redwood.rerank({
  query: 'find best match',
  candidates: [
    {id: 'cand-A', text: 'A'},
    {id: 'cand-B', text: 'B'},
    {id: 'cand-C', text: 'C'},
  ],
});
console.log(resp.candidates.map(c => ({id: c.id, score: c.score})))
// -> [{id:'cand-A', score:'9'},{id:'cand-B', score:'10'},{id:'cand-C', score:'2'}]
// ordering returned: B, A, C (customer expects B highest but with numeric compare 10>9>2)
```
sam-support: logs show server returned numeric scores: 10,9,2. Customer suspects TS SDK mis-parsing.
sam-support: attached server response JSON (from proxy logs):
```json
{"candidates":[{"id":"cand-B","score":10},{"id":"cand-A","score":9},{"id":"cand-C","score":2}]}
```

devin-sdk: I can repro quickly — thanks for details. My hunch: TS SDK does a string compare somewhere (we accidentally stringify scores during normalization).
devin-sdk: Quick repro I ran locally using our @latest TS SDK:
```ts
// SDK returns scores as strings in the client-side sorted output
> [{id:'cand-B', score:'10'}, {id:'cand-A', score:'9'}, {id:'cand-C', score:'2'}]
// But our sort function currently: candidates.sort((a,b) => String(b.score).localeCompare(String(a.score)))
// localeCompare yields '10' < '2' lexicographically? leads to odd ordering in edge cases
```
devin-sdk: So the bug is client-side only — server is fine. Python SDK doesn't have this codepath.
maria-ml: Good catch. Customer impact: ranking flip for multi-digit scores. If model returns integers >9, ordering may be wrong. Rare but bad for customers with raw scores not normalized to 0-1.
ryan-oncall: Severity? Customer reports production issue (e-commerce reorder). We should treat as P2 and patch quickly.
devin-sdk: Plan: change sort to numeric compare: (b.score as number) - (a.score as number). Also ensure when we build typed interfaces we keep score: number, not string. Add unit test with ["2","10","9"] case.
devin-sdk: I'll open a PR now, bump patch version, and cut release.
devin-sdk: Example fix (one-liner):
```ts
candidates.sort((a,b) => Number(b.score) - Number(a.score))
```

sam-support: Customer asked for short-term mitigation — can we suggest they normalize scores server-side to floats between 0 and 1? Or pin to Python SDK?
maria-ml: Recommend temp workaround: cast scores to number before client-side sorting. But we should push a patch ASAP.
ryan-oncall: Devin, estimate time to ship?
devin-sdk: PR in ~30m, CI + review ~2h. If nothing else pops, release in next deploy window. I'll also add a tiny telemetry event to see how many requests returned non-numeric types from backend.
deploy-bot: Scheduled patch deploy for ts-sdk v1.2.3 -> Canary in 1h, full rollout in 3h (pending CI + approvals). :rocket:

devin-sdk: Also adding a migration note in CHANGELOG and a support KB snippet showing how to detect this (inspect typeof candidate.score).
sam-support: I'll message the customer with repro explanation, short-term workaround (cast Number(score)), and ETA for fix.
ryan-oncall: Postmortem follow-ups: create unit test coverage for edge-case numeric/string mixes, add an integration test against proxy logs, and have product decide if we need to auto-coerce server numeric types.
maria-ml: Also check other SDKs (go/java) for similar patterns. Sounds like TS-specific but audit is quick.
devin-sdk: Will add tests and link the PR here when ready.
sam-support: Thanks team — customer updated to say they're okay waiting for the patch as long as we provide ETA. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
